item.research_question: How can interstitial carbon be utilized to unify multiple metallic strengthening mechanisms in a high-entropy alloy to achieve simultaneous high strength and ductility?
item.material_system: Fe49.5Mn30Co10Cr10C0.5 (at%) interstitial high-entropy alloy (iHEA), specifically a metastable TRIP-assisted dual-phase system with f.c.c. γ matrix and h.c.p. ε phase
item.processing_route: Vacuum induction melting of pure metals and carbon; hot-rolling at 900 °C (50% thickness reduction); homogenization at 1200 °C for 2 h in Ar followed by water-quenching; cold-rolling (60% reduction) and annealing at 900 °C for 3 min in Ar followed by water-quenching
item.test_conditions: Uniaxial tensile testing at room temperature (293 K) with an engineering strain rate of 1 × 10−3 s−1
key_findings: The grain-refined iHEA exhibits tensile strength nearly twice that of a single-phase equiatomic FeMnCoCrNi alloy while maintaining identical elongation.
The grain-refined iHEA shows ~100 MPa (~15%) higher yield and ultimate strength compared to a grain-refined TRIP-DP-HEA.
The fraction of transformed h.c.p. phase at the necking stage (εloc = 90%) is 36.5% (area%), indicating higher f.c.c. phase stability than substitutional TRIP-DP-HEAs (>75%).
Nano-twinning is observed as an essential additive deformation mechanism during early uniform deformation (εloc = 10%), unlike in TRIP-DP-HEAs where it occurs only later.
Nano-particles with an average size of 50~100 nm, identified as M23C6 carbides, are randomly distributed in the matrix with a volume fraction of ~1.5 vol.%.

The alloy unifies eight strengthening mechanisms: massive substitutional solid solution strengthening, interstitial solid solution strengthening, dual-phase composite effect, nano-particle strengthening, TWIP, TRIP, stacking fault formation, and grain size reduction.
The coarse-grained iHEA shows superior mechanical response with higher elongation and identical ultimate strength compared to a coarse-grained TRIP-DP-HEA.
item.mechanism: The addition of interstitial carbon increases the stacking fault energy and phase stability of the f.c.c. matrix, triggering a joint activation of twinning-induced plasticity (TWIP) and transformation-induced plasticity (TRIP) while maintaining the dual-phase structure. This is combined with massive substitutional and interstitial solid solution strengthening, Orowan strengthening from nano-carbides, and grain boundary strengthening from grain refinement.
item.limitations: The text does not explicitly state limitations of the study, though it notes that the true temperature during the short annealing time might be lower than the furnace temperature of 900 °C.
item.future_work: The authors propose that 'further optimization potential is at hand' due to the 'option for interstitial-driven tuning of phase (in)stability' and suggest that the design concept has 'very large potential to break the inverse strength-ductility relationship.'
quotes: The new interstitial TWIP-TRIP-HEA thus unifies all metallic strengthening mechanisms in one material, leading to twice the tensile strength compared to a single-phase HEA with similar composition, yet, at identical ductility.
Already during early uniform deformation (εloc = 10%), nano-twinning is observed in the iHEA as an essential additive deformation mechanism.
